//strict-note: This project's CANONICAL execution + test model is Node native type-stripping (no type
check at all — see package.json). `build` runs tsc purely to EMIT the dist/ + .d.ts
consumer artifact; it is deliberately non-strict because the .ts source is authored to the
type-stripping contract (erasable syntax), not to tsc's strict null / control-flow rules,
and those source files are owned/frozen (not editable from the build lane). A non-strict
emit compile is already STRICTER than the canonical zero-check runtime, and still fails on
real errors (missing imports, bad syntax, non-erasable TS). It just does not gate on
strictNullChecks pedantry over source it cannot change.
